clue.text: Report of injuries in this physics unit

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for injuries is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: hurts, as a noun, are injuries

explanation.surface: A news report about people injured in the physics department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' asks for the sound of HURTS; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of frequency, one cycle per second, named after Heinrich Hertz.

clue.text: Tree must be cut that has mark — a strategic move

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly
M is the abbreviation for the German mark
a tack is a change of course or approach, as in sailing

explanation.surface: A tree must be felled because it bears a mark, as part of some plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarack, a North American larch, also goes by this name.

clue.text: Takes pleasure in his leers naughtily

indicators.note: behaving naughtily, the letters misbehave and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a man's lecherous looks.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it keenly; the plural verb form matches 'Takes'.

clue.text: Island's unknown character I found in a Kiwi watering-hole

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so a letter standing for one is Z

indicators.note: I is said to be found inside the following phrase

parts.note: a Kiwi is a New Zealander, abbreviated NZ
a watering-hole is slang for a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A mysterious person turns up in a New Zealand pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts the lone I inside the pub phrase; the island's possessive 's is just a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An island off the coast of Tanzania in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Power brought by rank endlessly leading to anger

indicators.note: without its end, the synonym for rank loses its final letter

parts.note: a level is a rank or grade
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: An officer's rank brings power, and that leads to anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the word for rank; 'leading to' is only a positional link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is influence or advantage that lets one act effectively.

clue.text: Stars in synthetic fabric not cold

indicators.note: not cold means the abbreviation for cold is left out

parts.note: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic fabric
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Celebrities wearing stretchy man-made clothes in warm weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A constellation, the Lyre, containing the bright star Vega.

clue.text: Follows little girl, being there to offer protection

indicators.note: the word for being surrounds and shields the girl's name

parts.note: ens is the philosophical Latin word for being or entity
Sue is a short girl's name, from Susan

explanation.surface: Someone follows a young girl, on hand to protect her.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or result, a synonym for follow.

clue.text: Base dipso taken short when imbibing a litre

indicators.note: imbibing is drinking in, so the shortened drunk takes the other letters inside
made short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an alkie, like a dipso, is a heavy drinker

explanation.walkthrough: 'taken short' cuts ALKIE to ALKI; 'when imbibing' puts A L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a base that dissolves in water is an alkali, the opposite of an acid.

clue.text: Genuine article turning up outside front of Christie's

indicators.note: the reversed article sits outside the single letter
in a down clue turning up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: front of means just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A genuine antique turns up at the auction house Christie's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes EHT of THE; it goes round C.
explanation.definitionFit: German for real or authentic, used in English for something truly typical.

clue.text: Fellow passenger arriving perhaps in holed vessel

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
a lander is one who lands, as a passenger arriving by plane might

explanation.surface: A fellow traveller arriving on a ship full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl for draining food, so a vessel full of holes.

clue.text: Notice fibre lacking in English soldier who assists senior officer?

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: lacking in English means the abbreviation for English is dropped

parts.note: jute is a coarse plant fibre
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' removes E from JUTE to give JUT; the soldier is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is the officer who acts as administrative assistant to a commanding officer.

clue.text: Jock with a sports vehicle coming to a capital city

parts.note: a jock is short for disc jockey, a DJ
a kart is a small racing car used in karting

explanation.surface: A Scotsman drives a sports car into a capital.

clue.text: The old woman with dead dog

parts.note: one's old woman is one's mother, ma
a stiff is slang for a corpse, and stiff can mean dead

explanation.surface: An elderly lady and her dead pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Female isn't well, a female with little energy certain not to conk out

parts.note: someone who ails is unwell
E is the symbol for energy, a little part of the word

explanation.surface: A woman feeling poorly, with another woman short of energy.

clue.text: A mother's going to American university meeting Harvard's foremost economist

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother, here with its possessive s
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: foremost means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A mother's going off to an American university to meet Harvard's leading economist.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century Scottish author of The Wealth of Nations, founder of modern economics.

clue.text: Does what Tom cannot do and gets very cross

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, so it cannot give birth to young cats
an idiom for being very agitated or angry

explanation.surface: Someone does something beyond Tom and loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally only a queen cat can give birth, and figuratively the phrase means to be very upset.

clue.text: Natural liar uses manoeuvres — it's a game

indicators.note: the letters are manoeuvred, moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A born liar uses tactics; it's all a game to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A football code played on oval fields, chiefly in Australia.

clue.text: Soldiers getting stuck in remained in position taken earlier?

indicators.note: the soldiers are stuck inside the verb for remained

parts.note: rested means stayed or remained
OR is the abbreviation for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers get stuck in while others stayed put.

clue.text: Enjoy life without a mounting burden — this can free things up!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb goes round the rest

parts.note: to live is to enjoy life fully

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tax is a burden

clue.text: Fix vehicle for Spooner to get going

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to stick is to fix in place
a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: Mend the car so you can set off.

clue.text: Rough path gets reported

explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture or manner.

clue.text: Small lake coming into view

indicators.note: the lake comes into the word for view

parts.note: a sight is a view

clue.text: Draw an area for the audience

a playing card of the black suit marked with a trefoil

definitions.meaning: inspiration is literally drawing in air, so one who does it
